title: Avisa Residences: the promise of a growing township.
videoTitle: PROPERTY REVIEW #367 | AVISA RESIDENCES, TROPICANA ALAM PUNCAK ALAM
excerpt: A double-storey terrace on individual title, planned with the discipline of a strata scheme — arriving at a moment when the highways, the university and the shops are already finished.
takeaways: Individual-title terrace houses inside a guarded, single-entry master plan.
Highways, UiTM and shops are already in place in Puncak Alam.
Leasehold title and factories across the road are the main trade-offs.

sections.heading: What sets it apart
paragraphs: Avisa Residences is phase one of Tropicana Alam: 911 double-storey terrace houses on 88 acres with individual titles, yet a single guarded way in and out. Spine roads mean no house faces a junction, and there is a five-acre lake and parks.

The 20 by 70 ft Type A has 1,917 sq ft and four bedrooms, including a ground-floor bedroom with a ramped bathroom for older parents, and a family hall about 6.1 metres high that brings light into the middle of the house. Intermediate units were from about RM600,000; corner units, where every bedroom has its own bathroom, about RM900,000.

sections.heading: Where it is
paragraphs: It is in Puncak Alam beside the UiTM campus and hospital, among established townships such as City of Elmina, Bandar Seri Coalfields and Gamuda Gardens, with the GCE, DASH and WCE highways nearby. Factories are going up across the road.

pros: The terrace house Malaysians love, with an individual title, set in a master plan with a lake, parks, a single guarded entry, spine roads and perimeter fencing, from a developer whose earlier Tropicana Aman phases show the same consistency. Owners can extend as they like, which makes corner lots especially desirable.
The timing: the highways, UiTM, the hospital and shops are already there, so by handover in two or three years the area won't feel unfinished, a complaint buyers of earlier nearby projects had.
Competitive pricing: at the edge of the developable land, it undercuts other new projects while offering both the freedom of an individual title and a guardhouse, parks and privacy.
cons: Leasehold title, which matters to many landed buyers, and an individual-title format whose back lanes stay bare and whose look will fragment as owners renovate.
Industrial lots across the road mean heavy vehicles and possible noise, though also jobs and less competing housing; choose your orientation carefully.
So many projects nearby that, at RM600,000 to RM700,000, buyers have a lot of homework comparing them.

closing: Good value for a guarded, individual-title terrace house in a maturing area, if leasehold and the neighbouring factories don't put you off.
sourceNote: Based on Sean's full English captions for this February 2025 episode. The 3 on 3 follows the three things he likes and the three he doesn't, in his order, at the end of the video. The developer's team showed Sean around.
